name: Texas

sources.label: TEA — 19 TAC Chapter 74, Subchapter B: Graduation Requirements (August 2026 update)

plans.name: Foundation High School Program

subjects.label: English Language Arts
subjects.notes: English I, II, and III plus one more English course

subjects.label: Mathematics
subjects.notes: Must include Algebra I and Geometry

subjects.label: Science
subjects.notes: Must include Biology and one lab course such as IPC, Chemistry, or Physics

subjects.label: Social Studies
subjects.notes: U.S. History, half a credit of U.S. Government, half a credit of personal financial literacy, and one of World History, World Geography, or Foundations of Economics. Students who started 9th grade before 2026-27 take a half credit of economics and World History or World Geography instead.

subjects.label: Languages Other Than English
subjects.notes: Two credits in computer programming languages can also count

plans.notes: Includes 5 elective credits. Students are expected to also earn an endorsement; graduating with the Foundation program alone needs a parent's written permission after the student's sophomore year. Students who started 9th grade between 2014-15 and 2025-26 need the same credit totals; only their social studies course choices differ.

plans.name: Foundation + Endorsement

subjects.label: English Language Arts
subjects.notes: English I, II, and III plus one more English course

subjects.label: Mathematics
subjects.notes: Algebra I, Geometry, and two more math credits

subjects.label: Science
subjects.notes: Biology, a lab course, and two more science credits

plans.notes: Adds a 4th math credit, a 4th science credit, and 2 more electives to the Foundation program (7 electives total). Students finish the course pattern for at least one endorsement: STEM, Business and Industry, Public Services, Arts and Humanities, or Multidisciplinary Studies. Endorsement courses usually come from the elective credits.

plans.name: Distinguished Level of Achievement

subjects.label: English Language Arts
subjects.notes: English I, II, and III plus one more English course

subjects.label: Mathematics
subjects.notes: Must include Algebra I, Geometry, and Algebra II

plans.notes: Same as Foundation + Endorsement, but the four math credits must include Algebra II. At least one endorsement is required.

otherRequirements: Pass five state end-of-course exams: Algebra I, English I, English II, Biology, and U.S. History
Submit the FAFSA or TASFA financial aid application before graduating, unless a parent, an adult student, or a school counselor signs an opt-out
Starting with students enrolled in 2026-27, choose whether to share records for the state's direct college admission program (or turn in an opt-out form)
Show speaking and communication skills, as judged by the school district
districtNote: These are the Texas state minimums. Districts may require more, and each district decides which endorsement course sequences and advanced courses it offers, so check your district's graduation plan.
